Turnover increased marginally while operating profit was better than last year due to volumes sold despite the low prices. The cost of doing business however continues to be a major concern even as a consensus is yet to be reached with the labour unions on the 2014 and 2015 wage rates. During the period under review, the Kenya Shilling weakened slightly against the major currencies compared to prior year thus boosting the net realisations. The Company is also grappling with the uncertainty on the Land ownership under the Current Constitution due to Foreign ownership restrictions. We however hope that the National Government will give clear guidance on the leases through National Land Commission. PROSPECTS There are no indications of the global tea market picking up in the near future. As the weather continues to be favourable, we expect that the crop and stock levels will continue to rise depressing the tea prices further. The County Governments have prepared their budgets which appear to impose more taxes on firms operating within their juridictions. The labour unions are pressing for higher wages despite the economic conditions currently prevailing in the tea sector. The Board continues to look into cost effective ways of running the Company operations under the circustamces even as the remaining months to year end are likely to more challenging. PROFIT WARNING Based on the above stated factors and in accordance with Regulations G.05(1) (f) and (2) of the Capital markets Securities and Public Offers and Listings and Disclosures Regulations, 2002, the second half of the year results are unlikely to attain results close to last year's levels. It is therefore reasonable at this time to to anticipate earnings for the financial year ending March 2015 to be lower than the previous year's earnings by at least 25%.
